findings.deletion_test: Retain the TLS, OCSP, and certificate-related reliability focus; narrow the categorical uptime comparison.
findings.diagnosis: The claim promises continued availability whenever competing servers fail from these broad issue classes, without identifying the failures or conditions it covers.
findings.evidence: Lines 85–86 identify cluster coordination and multi-issuer fallback, but those capabilities do not establish immunity to all TLS, OCSP, or certificate-related outages.
findings.quote: **Stays up when other servers go down** due to TLS/OCSP/certificate-related issues

findings.deletion_test: Retain extensibility, the architecture link, and the modular design; remove or bound the unlimited capability and unconditional efficiency claims.
findings.diagnosis: “Anything without bloat” turns a concrete architectural property into an unlimited capability claim with an undefined resource-cost guarantee.
findings.evidence: Line 177 describes applications implemented as Caddy modules, and line 179 names specific benefits. Neither establishes unlimited functionality or an absence of overhead.
findings.quote: **Highly extensible** [modular architecture](https://caddyserver.com/docs/architecture) lets Caddy do anything without bloat
findings.source_function: Explain the benefit of modular extensibility.

findings.deletion_test: Preserve the concrete claim about external dependencies, including libc; bound the deployment scope.
findings.diagnosis: “Runs anywhere” equates dependency independence with universal platform compatibility, although those are different properties.
findings.evidence: The adjoining qualification concerns external dependencies only. Line 120 acknowledges operating-system-specific execution requirements, and the page provides no universal platform scope.
findings.quote: **Runs anywhere** with **no external dependencies** (not even libc)

findings.deletion_test: Retain that Caddy is written in Go and the intended memory-safety benefit; correct or delimit the comparison class.
findings.diagnosis: The comparison mixes a language's guarantees with those of unspecified server implementations and implies superiority over other servers generally.
findings.evidence: The page identifies Caddy's implementation language but does not identify competing implementation languages or distinguish servers with equivalent memory-safety guarantees.
findings.quote: Written in Go, a language with higher **memory safety guarantees** than other servers

findings.deletion_test: The promotional lead can be removed without losing a feature or destination; preserve access to the features page through its existing heading link.
findings.diagnosis: This feature-list item supplies no feature or qualification and repeats navigation already provided by the section heading.
findings.evidence: Line 76 links “Features” to the same https://caddyserver.com/features destination.

findings.deletion_test: Preserve the following explanation about configuring initialized types and its HTTP, TLS, and storage examples; remove or delimit the universal ranking.
findings.diagnosis: The sentence claims superiority over every existing web server without defining a comparative measure of control.
findings.evidence: The next sentence explains a specific configuration mechanism, qualified by “usually.” That mechanism does not establish the preceding universal ranking.
findings.quote: Caddy exposes an unprecedented level of control compared to any web server in existence.
findings.source_function: Introduce the configuration model's degree of control.

findings.deletion_test: Retain plugin-based extensibility; remove or specify the comparative improvement claim.
findings.diagnosis: “Vast improvements over other web servers” asserts a large comparative advantage without identifying which properties improve or which servers are compared.
findings.evidence: The paragraph explains direct configuration of initialized types but names no plugin-system comparison or measurable improvement. Line 92 already identifies modular extensibility.
findings.quote: Caddy is also ridiculously extensible, with a powerful plugin system that makes vast improvements over other web servers.

findings.deletion_test: Remove the repeated introduction while retaining the documentation URL and the separate contribution information.
findings.diagnosis: This sentence repeats the immediately preceding heading and merely announces the immediately following link.
findings.evidence: Line 192 says “Full documentation,” line 196 provides the documentation URL, and line 198 supplies the independently useful contribution information.

findings.deletion_test: Preserve the sponsorship request, project-funding rationale, and concrete support benefits; remove or qualify the predicted audience reaction.
findings.diagnosis: The clause presents a favorable reaction from customers and prospective customers as an assured sponsorship benefit.
findings.evidence: The paragraph identifies funding, private help, resources, support, and discounts, but provides no condition connecting sponsorship to customer awareness or approval.
findings.quote: along with being a great look for your company to your customers and potential customers!
findings.source_function: Persuade companies to sponsor the project.

findings.deletion_test: Retain Cloudsmith's hosting credit, URL, and concrete package-management functions; remove or bound the exclusivity, format, destination, and confidence guarantees.
findings.diagnosis: The sponsor description combines an exclusive market claim with unrestricted format and destination coverage and an unconditional assurance. These exceed the concrete service role established on the page.
findings.evidence: The preceding sentence establishes that Cloudsmith provides Debian package repository hosting. It supplies no comparison class for “only” or scope for “any format” and “any place”; the claims are also not attributed as Cloudsmith's own.
findings.quote: Cloudsmith is the only fully hosted, cloud-native, universal package management solution, that enables your organization to create, store and share packages in any format, to any place, with total confidence.
